title: Junkers Ju 88 A-4 (IL-2)

sources.title: JoyPro cockpit catalog (from the IL-2 and real aircraft manuals)

intro: The Ju 88 was a German medium bomber that could also dive-bomb. Four crew sit together in the nose compartment: the pilot at the front left with the bomb aimer next to him. Throttles and propeller controls are on the left console; the dive system runs from the dive brake lever and the bomb release button on the yoke.

areas.name: Gunsight
areas.text: The reflector sight and the dive angle lines are in front of the pilot.

panels.name: Revi C12/D gunsight and dive lines
panels.text: This is the reflector gunsight in front of the pilot. A glass plate shows an aiming mark that seems to float in the air; the pilot puts the mark on the target to aim the guns.
panels.context: The pilot uses it in every attack. The knob dims the mark and the lever swings a sun filter in front of the glass. Lines on the side window show the dive angle.

controls.name: Reflector glass
controls.text: This is the glass plate of the reflector gunsight. It shows an aiming mark; the pilot moves the mark onto the target to aim the guns.
controls.context: The mark looks as if it floats in the air in front of the plane.

controls.name: Sight dimmer
controls.text: This knob sets how bright the aiming mark of the gunsight glows.
controls.context: The pilot turns it down in dim light and up in bright light so the mark stays easy to see.

controls.name: Sun filter
controls.text: This lever swings a tinted filter in front of the gunsight glass, like sunglasses for the sight.
controls.context: The pilot uses it when looking toward the sun, so the aiming mark does not get lost in the glare.

controls.name: Dive angle markings
controls.text: These are lines on the side window. They show the dive angle when the horizon is lined up with one of them.
controls.context: The pilot uses them during dive attacks together with the dive brake lever.

areas.name: Instrument panel
areas.text: The flight instruments are on the upper left, the engine gauges on the right and the fuel panel low on the right.

panels.name: Instrument panel
panels.text: This is the main panel. The flight instruments are on the upper left, the engine gauges for both engines on the right and the fuel panel low on the right.
panels.context: The pilot watches both engines. The bomb aimer shares the compartment.

controls.name: Homing indicator
controls.text: This instrument has a needle that swings left or right toward a homing beacon, a radio station on the ground. The pilot turns the plane toward the needle.
controls.context: It helps the crew to find the way back to their airfield, even in bad weather.

controls.name: Variometer (climb and descent indicator)
controls.text: This dial shows how fast the plane climbs or sinks.
controls.context: The pilot watches it to hold a steady climb or descent.

controls.name: Turn and slip indicator
controls.text: This instrument has a needle that shows how fast the plane turns and a ball that shows whether it skids sideways. The pilot keeps the ball in the middle with the rudder.
controls.context: It is one of the basic flight instruments, used in clouds and for turning.

controls.name: Artificial horizon
controls.text: This dial shows a small plane in front of a line that stands for the true horizon. It tilts like the real plane, so it shows whether the nose points up or down and whether the wings are level.
controls.context: The pilot relies on it in cloud, at night and in dives, when the real horizon cannot be seen.

controls.name: Compass
controls.text: This is the magnetic compass. It shows the direction the plane is heading, like a hiking compass.
controls.context: The pilot uses it to hold a course.

controls.name: Dive angle / bank indicator
controls.text: The catalog names this instrument dive angle / bank indicator and describes a slip ball that the pilot keeps in the middle with the rudder. Nothing more is known about it.
controls.context: It sits among the flight instruments on the upper left of the Ju 88 panel.

controls.name: Directional gyro
controls.text: This is a compass steadied by a gyroscope (a fast-spinning wheel). It is easier to read in turns than a magnetic compass. The pilot sets it to the magnetic compass from time to time.
controls.context: The pilot uses it for holding a heading, especially during long flights.

controls.name: Airspeed indicator
controls.text: This dial shows how fast the plane moves through the air. The scale is in kilometres per hour (km/h).
controls.context: The pilot watches it all the time. Too slow and the wings stop carrying the plane; too fast and the plane can be damaged. It matters most at take-off and landing.

controls.name: Altimeter
controls.text: This dial shows how high the plane is, measured from the air pressure. The needles work like the hands of a clock, one for the hundreds and one for the thousands of metres.
controls.context: The pilot checks it to stay clear of the ground and to hold the height the mission needs.

controls.name: Course indicator (PDI)
controls.text: This instrument has a needle that shows how far the plane is off its course. The pilot steers until the needle is in the middle.
controls.context: It is used with the radio when the pilot homes in on a beacon or flies a set course.

controls.name: Altimeter (second one)
controls.text: This dial shows how high the plane is, measured from the air pressure. The needles work like the hands of a clock, one for the hundreds and one for the thousands of metres. The catalog lists this a second time; this entry is the second one.
controls.context: The pilot checks it to stay clear of the ground and to hold the height the mission needs. (Second entry of the same kind.)

controls.name: Fuel pressure gauge
controls.text: This dial shows the pressure of the fuel. In the First World War planes it shows the pressure in the fuel tank that pushes the fuel to the engine.
controls.context: If the pressure drops, the pilot pumps it up again with the hand pump.

controls.name: Landing gear lights
controls.text: These lamps show where the landing gear is. The catalog says red means up and green means down.
controls.context: The pilot checks them before landing to see that the wheels are really down.

controls.name: Clock
controls.text: This is the flight clock. It has a stopwatch for timing parts of the flight.
controls.context: The pilot times legs of the route with it and checks how long the fuel has to last.

controls.name: Directional gyro (second one)
controls.text: This is a compass steadied by a gyroscope (a fast-spinning wheel). It is easier to read in turns than a magnetic compass. The pilot sets it to the magnetic compass from time to time. The catalog lists this a second time; this entry is the second one.
controls.context: The pilot uses it for holding a heading, especially during long flights. (Second entry of the same kind.)

controls.name: Boost (manifold pressure) gauge (left engine)
controls.text: This dial shows the boost, the pressure with which the supercharger pushes air into the engine. More boost means more engine power. This entry is the left engine one.
controls.context: The throttle sets the boost. The pilot watches it so that the engine is not pushed beyond what it can take. This entry covers the left engine.

controls.name: Boost (manifold pressure) gauge (right engine)
controls.text: This dial shows the boost, the pressure with which the supercharger pushes air into the engine. More boost means more engine power. This entry is the right engine one.
controls.context: The throttle sets the boost. The pilot watches it so that the engine is not pushed beyond what it can take. This entry covers the right engine.

controls.name: Tachometer (left engine)
controls.text: This dial shows how fast the engine turns, in revolutions per minute (RPM). This entry is the left engine one.
controls.context: The pilot watches it all the time to keep the engine in its safe range. This entry covers the left engine.

controls.name: Tachometer (right engine)
controls.text: This dial shows how fast the engine turns, in revolutions per minute (RPM). This entry is the right engine one.
controls.context: The pilot watches it all the time to keep the engine in its safe range. This entry covers the right engine.

controls.name: Oil and fuel pressure gauge (both engines)
controls.text: This double dial shows the oil and fuel pressure of both engines.
controls.context: A drop in either pressure warns of engine trouble. The pilot glances at it often.

controls.name: Coolant temperature gauge (left engine)
controls.text: This dial shows the temperature of the liquid that cools the engine. The pilot opens or closes the radiators to keep it in the safe range. This entry is the left engine one.
controls.context: A reading that climbs too high warns of overheating. This is why the radiator controls are close to hand. This entry covers the left engine.

controls.name: Coolant temperature gauge (right engine)
controls.text: This dial shows the temperature of the liquid that cools the engine. The pilot opens or closes the radiators to keep it in the safe range. This entry is the right engine one.
controls.context: A reading that climbs too high warns of overheating. This is why the radiator controls are close to hand. This entry covers the right engine.

controls.name: System indicator
controls.text: The catalog lists this as a further system indicator, named so in the IL-2 guide. Nothing more is known about it.
controls.context: It sits among the instruments of the cockpit.

controls.name: System indicator (second one)
controls.text: The catalog lists this as a further system indicator, named so in the IL-2 guide. Nothing more is known about it. The catalog lists this a second time; this entry is the second one.
controls.context: It sits among the instruments of the cockpit. (Second entry of the same kind.)

controls.name: Fuel contents gauge
controls.text: This dial shows how much fuel is left in the tanks.
controls.context: The pilot checks it often to know how long the plane can still fly.

controls.name: Fuel gauge selector
controls.text: This switch selects which tank the fuel contents gauge shows, so one gauge can report on several tanks.
controls.context: The pilot turns it to look at each tank in turn.

controls.name: Fuel contents gauge (second one)
controls.text: This dial shows how much fuel is left in the tanks. The catalog lists this a second time; this entry is the second one.
controls.context: The pilot checks it often to know how long the plane can still fly. (Second entry of the same kind.)

controls.name: Outside air temperature gauge
controls.text: This dial shows the temperature of the air outside the plane.
controls.context: The crew reads from it how cold it is at the height of the plane.

controls.name: TAS selector
controls.text: This switch works with the true airspeed indicator (TAS means true airspeed). The catalog says it switches that indicator.
controls.context: It sits next to the true airspeed indicator on the Ju 88 panel.

controls.name: True airspeed indicator
controls.text: This dial shows the true airspeed, the actual speed of the plane through the air. At height it is higher than the airspeed indicator shows.
controls.context: The crew uses it for navigation, to work out where the plane will be.

areas.name: Left console
areas.text: Throttles, propeller pitch controls, dive brake lever, trim wheels, flaps and gear are on the left.

panels.name: Left console
panels.text: This is the left console with the throttle levers, the propeller pitch switches, the dive brake lever, the trim wheels, the flap control, the gear control and the radiator controls.
panels.context: The pilot's left hand works these controls.

controls.name: Throttle levers
controls.text: These levers make the engines stronger or weaker, like the gas pedal of a car. There is one for each engine.
controls.context: They sit on the left console. On a twin-engined plane the pilot moves both together and one by one to turn.

controls.name: Propeller pitch switches
controls.text: These switches change the propeller pitch by hand, which means how sharply the blades bite the air. Pressing the switch changes the engine speed.
controls.context: The pilot sets the pitch for take-off, climb and cruise. The He 111 catalog adds that feathering is possible.

controls.name: Dive brake lever
controls.text: This lever extends the dive brakes, big flaps that stop the plane from getting too fast in a steep dive.
controls.context: The pilot uses it for dive attacks. It sits on the left console next to the throttles.

controls.name: Trim handwheels (elevator, rudder, aileron)
controls.text: These three handwheels trim the plane on all three axes: up and down (elevator), left and right (rudder), and roll (aileron). Trim is a small adjustment so the plane flies straight without the pilot holding the controls.
controls.context: On a heavy bomber the pilot trims the plane for the long flight so that it holds its attitude by itself.

controls.name: Flap control
controls.text: This lever raises and lowers the flaps in two stages. Flaps are parts of the wing that slide out to give more lift at low speed.
controls.context: The pilot lowers them for take-off and landing and raises them in normal flight.

controls.name: Landing gear control
controls.text: This control raises and lowers the landing gear, the wheels and their legs. The gear folds away in flight.
controls.context: The pilot lowers it before landing and raises it after take-off.

controls.name: Radiator controls
controls.text: These handles open and close the flaps of the radiators. The radiators use the passing air to cool the engines.
controls.context: The pilot opens them when an engine gets hot and closes them for less drag.

areas.name: Bomb controls
areas.text: The bomb release panel, the bombsight and the emergency jettison are on the right.

panels.name: Bomb controls
panels.text: These controls handle the bombs: the release selector, the Lotfe 7 bombsight in the gondola and the emergency jettison handle.
panels.context: The bomb aimer works the sight for level bombing.

controls.name: Bomb release selector
controls.text: This selector chooses how the bombs leave the plane: one at a time (single), one after another in a row (series) or all together (salvo). The catalog lists single and salvo for the Ju 87 and single, series and salvo for the Ju 88 and He 111.
controls.context: The pilot or bomb aimer sets it before the attack. The release button on the control column or yoke then drops the bombs the chosen way.

controls.name: Lotfe 7 bombsight
controls.text: This is the Lotfe 7 bombsight, the telescope the bomb aimer in the gondola uses to aim bombs in level flight.
controls.context: The bomb aimer lines up the target in the sight and the bombs are released at the right moment.

controls.name: Emergency jettison handle
controls.text: Pulling this handle drops the bombs at once, without the normal release.
controls.context: The pilot uses it in an emergency, for example when the plane must get lighter fast or the normal release does not work.

areas.name: Control column and throttle
areas.text: These are the controls on the pilot's stick or yoke and on the left-hand throttle side that JoyPro can assign to a joystick or throttle.

panels.name: Control column and yoke
panels.text: This is the control column with its yoke or wheel and the buttons on it.
panels.context: The pilot flies with it; on the bombers the bomb release is on it.

controls.name: Control column with yoke
controls.text: This is the control column with a wheel or yoke. Pushing and pulling it tilts the plane's nose down and up, turning the wheel rolls the plane. In the game: pitch: Pitch; roll: Roll.
controls.context: It is the pilot's main flight control. On the larger planes it replaces the stick.

controls.name: Bomb release button
controls.text: This button on the yoke drops the bombs. It lets the pilot release them without the bomb aimer. In the game: press: Release bombs; ends the dive.
controls.context: It works only when bombs are carried.

controls.name: Forward gun trigger
controls.text: This button on the yoke fires the fixed forward machine gun. In the game: press: Fire the fixed forward MG.
controls.context: The pilot uses it to shoot at targets ahead of the plane.

panels.name: Throttle and left-hand controls
panels.text: These are the throttle levers and other controls the pilot's left hand reaches on the left side of the cockpit.
panels.context: The pilot sets engine power, trim, flaps and gear with the left hand.

controls.name: Left throttle
controls.text: This is the throttle of the left engine. It makes that engine stronger or weaker. In the game: axis: Left engine power (boost).
controls.context: On a twin-engined plane the pilot moves both throttles together for straight flight and one at a time to turn on the ground.

controls.name: Right throttle
controls.text: This is the throttle of the right engine. It makes that engine stronger or weaker. In the game: axis: Right engine power (boost).
controls.context: Holding one throttle back while the other stays open helps to steer on the ground and to fly straight when the engines pull unevenly.

controls.name: Propeller pitch controls
controls.text: This sets the engine speed (RPM) through the propeller pitch, which means how sharply the propeller blades bite the air. In the game: axis: Set engine RPM.
controls.context: Together with the throttle it sets the power of the engines. The pilot moves it forward for take-off and back for cruising.

controls.name: Dive brake lever
controls.text: This lever extends and retracts the dive brakes, big flaps that stop the plane from getting too fast in a steep dive. In the game: fwd: Extend dive brakes (starts the dive); aft: Retract dive brakes.
controls.context: The pilot moves it forward to begin a dive attack and back to put the brakes away.

controls.name: Elevator trim wheel
controls.text: This handwheel trims the plane. Trim is a small adjustment so the plane flies level without the pilot holding the controls. In the game: up: Trim nose down; down: Trim nose up.
controls.context: The pilot turns it after take-off and when speed or load changes.

controls.name: Flap control
controls.text: This control raises and lowers the flaps. Flaps are parts of the wing that slide out to give more lift at low speed. In the game: up: Flaps up; down: Flaps down (two stages).
controls.context: On the throttle side of the HOTAS, this is the flap lever of the left console; it is moved down for take-off and landing and up after that.

controls.name: Landing gear control
controls.text: This control raises and lowers the landing gear, the wheels and their legs. In the game: up: Gear up; down: Gear down.
controls.context: The pilot moves it down before landing and up after take-off, then checks the gear lights.
